title: The lens cluster and triod cluster uniquely minimize the anisotropic perimeter in $\mathbb{R}^2$
summary: (N, M)-clusters are partitions of $\mathbb{R}^d$ into N+M regions, where N chambers have prescribed finite measure and M chambers have infinite measure. Locally minimizing clusters are the configurations which minimize the perimeter among all competitors with compact support satisfying the same measure constraints. The characterization of these partitions has been widely studied for the standard (isotropic) perimeter.
